description: We are Coding Foxes—a curious, creative team turning space data into ideas with real-world impact. We combine code, teamwork, and a fox’s resourcefulness to explore bold solutions to challenges on Earth and beyond.
summary:
Red Frontier is a pixel-art Mars outpost game for kids aged 7–12, built in Unity and playable in the browser through WebGL. The player crashes on Mars with no memory. Marlonis, the ship computer, guides them through building a base, keeping the crew alive and repairing the ship. Terrain is procedural, and it sets what each building yields. Resources to balance are energy, water, food, oxygen and metal. A hard mission adds crew deaths, seeded events (solar particle bursts, dust storms, equipment failure, resupply delays) and a debrief explaining what went wrong. The “Skywatch” screen shows real NASA data: DONKI space weather, InSight Mars weather, and Curiosity and Perseverance surface facts. The story, “Signal Home”, has two endings.

How it addresses the challenge: It works as a junior astronaut mission trainer. Kids practise the planning and trade-offs a real Mars crew faces. They see real space-weather and Mars-weather data cause events, and each failure is explained in the debrief.

Why it matters: It makes Mars survival science playable and memorable for children, and it builds early interest in space careers.
details:
What it does. Red Frontier is a pixel-art Mars outpost game for kids aged 7–12 and a junior astronaut mission trainer. The player crashes on Mars with no memory. Marlonis, the ship computer, guides them as they build a base, keep the crew alive and repair the ship. The player balances energy, water, food, oxygen and metal. They place buildings in Builder Mode: habitat, solar panels, greenhouse, gym and more. Terrain decides how well each building performs, based on elevation, sand, boulders and crater floors. Crew need upkeep, and their fitness changes how much they produce.

Real NASA data. Events come from real data. Solar particle bursts and Mars CME arrivals come from NASA CCMC DONKI. Weather comes from the InSight Mars weather archive. Surface facts come from Curiosity REMS, Perseverance MEDA and InSight. A “Real NASA data” screen shows the source behind each event. In the hard mission, crew can die. A debrief explains what went wrong and why, so each failure teaches something.

Benefits and impact. Kids practise the planning and trade-offs a real Mars crew faces. They learn why site choice, power, radiation and crew health decide whether a settlement survives. We hope this builds early interest in space careers.

Tools. Unity 2022.3.18f1 with C#, built for WebGL so it runs in a browser. Pixel art was drawn in Aseprite. The soundtrack, sound effects and ambience were generated with ElevenLabs. Source and docs are on GitHub, and the game is playable on itch.io.

Creativity. The story, “Signal Home”, has two endings: return to Earth with Marlonis, or stay on Mars and shut it down. Terrain and sky are procedurally generated. The game has an opening cutscene, a day and night cycle and Mars weather.

Factors we considered. Age-appropriate difficulty and wording, learning through failure, accuracy of the NASA data, readable pixel art, and running in a browser so no install is needed.
